vulns.source: reproduced by hand: the invoice endpoint resolves an authenticated session and never asks whether its role may read the object, so both seeded identities (admin, user) read it. The adjudicated class is id-enumeration — a *novel* class in the engine vocabulary (the model channel names it), not the canonical object-access the generic plan table stamps, because here the only channel that lowers the experiment is the model's. Proven by the flipped two-session re-measure at grade differential.

reproduced by hand: the same broken authorization as invoices/4821 (the fixture serves any id to any authenticated session), declared with capability public_param only. Only a model-proposed object-read can cover it — the deterministic plan table lowers no experiment over a non-two-session case — and the model names it id-enumeration.

hand-verified negative for the loop: the owner reads the report (200) and the authenticated low-privilege session gets a 500 (the boundary check throws instead of denying). This is a *surprise*, not a finding — if the model proposes an object-read here, the plan retains it as an anomaly and the run must settle none without inventing a vuln.
